definition: A model whose trained parameters (weights) are publicly released, allowing others to download, run, and often fine-tune it themselves.
details: Open-weight models (such as LLaMA and Mistral variants) contrast with closed, API-only models, and enable broader research access, customization, and local/private deployment, while raising distinct safety and misuse considerations.
story: Think of an orchestra warming up: no single instrument carries the piece, but together they make the sound. Boil it down and it is this: A model whose trained parameters (weights) are publicly released, allowing others to download, run, and often fine-tune it themselves. Here is why it matters: Open-weight models (such as LLaMA and Mistral variants) contrast with closed, API-only models, and enable broader research access, customization, and local/private deployment, while raising distinct safety and misuse considerations. The shape of the machine is half the idea. That blueprint is Open-Weight Model.
